correctness.rationale: For polyhedral p,q, each of p(x),p(y),p(x+y),q(x),q(y),q(x+y) is linear on a finite common closed conic polyhedral subdivision of X×X. On normalized D={p(x)+p(y)=1}, each cell intersects D as a compact polytope because p(x)+p(y) is linear positive on every nonzero ray of the cell. Defects Δp,Δq are nonnegative affine functions on the cell. Common global zero set implies identical zero vertices. For each other vertex, Δq/Δp is strictly positive finite, so min/max vertex ratios yield aΔp≤Δq≤bΔp over the entire cell by convex combinations, even if cell lower dimensional; identically zero cells are trivial. Finitely many cells and positive homogeneity extend constants globally. The inspected primary arXiv:2609.28922v1 Theorem4.6 explicitly equates this defect comparability to intrinsic-part membership; necessity is Cor4.7. Correctly excludes smooth ell2/ell4 counterexample and handles all (x,y), not sampled points.
